From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@quantumlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Targeting Sprint — Decision Windows & Owner Roster

Team — launching the short targeting sprint for annual planning. Goal is to lock the decision windows for targets (base / upside / downside) and assign clear owners for each decision lane so we can feed tidy inputs into the QBR deck by June 10.

Quick context: after the product cohort review last week, we need a three-week push to finalize the trajectory playbook: scenario triggers, owner commitments, and the escalation path for any delta > 10% vs. baseline forecasts. I attached the initial playbook and owner roster.

Top asks for this thread (please respond inline):
- Confirm you own the lane(s) listed in owner-roster.csv and update if not.
- Capture 1–2 plausible downside triggers and 1 upside opportunity for your lane.
- Identify any blocking dependencies (people, data, security approvals) with ETA.

Proposed timeline:
- May 25: Align owners and decision windows (this thread).
- May 27: Initial scenario drafts due (short bullets).
- June 2: Consolidation + leadership dry run.
- June 10: QBR-ready slides delivered.

Notes: prioritize measurable triggers (metrics + threshold) over narratives. If you foresee a costly mitigation, flag it now so we can surface to finance.

Attachments: trajectory-playbook-v1.pdf (summary), owner-roster.csv (current assignments).

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Head of Strategic Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Targeting Sprint — Decision Windows & Owner Roster

Thanks Jonas — this looks good. A few clarifications from my side before owners lock in:

1) Decision windows: we need to define the cadence for re-eval (weekly vs. bi-weekly) for lanes that have noisy leading indicators (e.g., latency-driven revenue). I propose weekly for product-performance sensitive lanes, bi-weekly for sales/partner ramps.
2) Escalation path: if the downside trigger is hit, who signs off on the mitigation spend >$50k? Recommend Jason (finance) + me looped in.
3) Dependencies: we should treat capacity reallocation as a separate gating item — call out required GPU-months and expected cost impact.

I'll own synthesizing the cross-cutting dependencies and will add a short appendix to trajectory-playbook-v1 with decision cadence recommendations.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | COO
